5) Do you provide a signed attestation or evidence for erasure on request (e.g., for HIPAA compliance)?

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can paste into your questionnaire; I'm attaching a one-page blueprint and a retention matrix for your folder. If you'd like, Ben can add the snapshot/backup technical detail.

1) Region constraints: Yes. For Hosted API customers we support region pinning to a single cloud region (US-only regions: us-west-2, us-east-1, us-central-1). All primary data stores, in-transit replication, and short-term KV caches are provisioned in the selected region. Cross-region failover is an opt-in policy — by default we do not replicate data outside the pinned region.

2) Retention windows (defaults and options):
- Request logs (metrics/tracing): default 30 days; configurable 0–365 days via Console; exportable to customer-managed S3 for longer retention.
- Full request payloads (hosted API request/response bodies): default 7 days (ephemeral by default); options: 0 days (no persistence), 7, 30, 90 days. Longer retention requires Customer Agreement addendum.
- Embeddings/derived vectors: default 0 days (not stored unless customer enables storage using a named index); if enabled, retention follows the same 0/7/30/90 windows above.

3) Deletion/erasures workflow:
- Primary stores: deletes are synchronous at the service layer (API returns success once primary records are removed).
- Caches (in-memory/KV): cleared on delete event immediately; KV shards are garbage-collected within the same maintenance window (seconds-to-minutes).
- Backups/snapshots: deletion from snapshot storage is handled by background jobs (see snapshot policy below). We provide a documented purge confirmation once snapshot entries are removed.

4) Backups/snapshots retention and geography:
- Automated daily snapshots of customer-configured indices are retained for 14 days by default; configurable up to 90 days for Enterprise customers.
- Snapshots are stored encrypted at rest in the same cloud region by default; if a customer requests cross-region replication that is an explicit opt-in and will be clearly called out in the contract.

5) Attestation/evidence:
- We supply evidence packages for erasure requests on an as-needed basis (audit log extract + snapshot deletion confirmation). For HIPAA/enterprise customers we provide a documented attestation describing the deletion steps and dates.

Attachments: HostedAPI_DataHandling_Blueprint.pdf; RetentionMatrix.csv

Hi Alex — Ben here, engineering on runtime and storage. Quick technical clarifications to address A/B: 

A) Envelope encryption model: snapshots and object backups are encrypted with envelope encryption. By default we use Redwood-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS) scoped to the customer's region. On Enterprise plans we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) — the key ID can be specified in the Console and used for snapshot encryption. Key rotation follows AWS best practices; we provide rotation audit entries for compliance.

B) Restore semantics and deletions: snapshots are immutable point-in-time objects. However, our restore tooling applies deletion markers (tombstones) at restore time if a legal erasure request exists for an object within the requested timeframe. Practically: if Sentinel requests erasure on 2028-08-20 for object X, and a snapshot from 2028-07-01 includes X, a subsequent restore will not reintroduce X into active stores — our restore process checks for erasure markers and skips rehydrating tombstoned items. We also maintain audit logs showing that the object was skipped during restore.

I've dropped a short Summary text file into the evidence folder (Snapshot_Retention_Summary.txt). Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk the legal/engineering teams through the flow.

Thanks,
